# Module `url`

url - URL parsing in pure Vyb (no FFI).

Splits a single absolute URL into (scheme, host, port, path), resolving the
scheme's conventional default port when the URL omits one, so a caller can
pick the http vs https client from the scheme and pass port/path straight
through.

This is the stdlib promotion of the behavior-verified framework parser
(VybOS `modules/url.vyb`, which drives every realizer slice); it is kept
behavior-identical.

Usage:
  import url::{url_split, default_port, UrlSplit}
  u<UrlSplit> = url_split("https://codeload.github.com:8443/vim/vim/tar.gz")
  # u.scheme == "https", u.host == "codeload.github.com", u.port == 8443,
  # u.path  == "/vim/vim/tar.gz"

Note: IPv6 bracket hosts (`[::1]:8080`) and URL fragments (`#frag`) are NOT
specially handled; a host containing `:` is split at the first colon and a
fragment is captured as part of the path.

### `default_port` · fn


The conventional default port for a scheme name, classified with a
single-value String `select`. Unknown / empty schemes fall to the wildcard.

<a id="sym-url_split"></a>
### `url_split` · fn

```
url_split(raw<String>)<UrlSplit> ->
```

Split a raw absolute URL string into its components, resolving the default
port. A leading scheme (`scheme://`) is honoured; a bare host/port or
host:path input defaults the scheme to "http". A string with no scheme and no
authority (`hello`) is treated as a host-only reference.
